newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia coffee trade waiting on trucker strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombia coffee trade waiting on trucker strike.

text.p: Colombia's main truck drivers' union has said it will forge ahead with plans to stage a nationwide strike from April 20 after its latest round of talks with the government failed to narrow differences over key demands.
"There's no other option but a stoppage," Javier Suarez, president of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC) said in a statement to the union's rank-and-file late Tuesday.
The statement was issued after Suarez and other senior union officials held closed-door talks with Transportation Minister Carlos Lopez.
Olga Rosero, the ACC's sectional chief for central Cundinamarca province of which Bogota is the capital, said the talks -- billed as a last-ditch attempt to avert a work stoppage -- had led nowhere.

The ACC, which represents about 80 percent of Colombia's truckers, called the April 20 stoppage in March to protest what it describes as the abject failure by private transportation companies and the government to live up to terms of an agreement that ended a crippling 11-day strike last October.
That strike paralyzed virtually all of the country's road freight including about 200,000 60-kg bags of coffee.

In addition to higher freight rates, the October accord included a promise of extra payments to truckers waiting to on- and off-load goods and a pledge from the government to revise vehicle licensing fees and highway tolls.
Union officials say the ACC is now demanding the resignation of Lopez, and a curb on the number of cargo vehicles operating across the country, as part of any deal to avert the April 20 strike.

Private coffee exporters are still less than apprehensive about news of the impending strike, since the deadline for the job action is more than a week away. One exporter stressed that a strike starting April 20 would have to hold for at least 10 days before it would have any impact on coffee export schedules.
A spokesman for the Transporation Ministry said, meanwhile, that the government was confident about the possibility of working out an agreement before April 20.
"The minister has appointed a commission headed by the deputy minister, the director of transit and the deputy director of cargo to continue negotiating," he said.
